html:
Francisco de Paula Santander was a general of Colombian independence and the first great builder of its state. He was vice-president of Gran Colombia and president of New Granada from 1832 to 1837.

He fought beside Bolívar and commanded the vanguard at the Battle of Boyacá. While Bolívar campaigned in Peru, Santander ran Gran Colombia from Bogotá, founding schools and enforcing the laws, which earned him the name Man of Laws.

The two men fell out over Bolívar's wish for a strong presidency. After a failed attempt on Bolívar's life in 1828, Santander was accused, condemned and exiled. He came back as president when the union broke up. He is seen as the founder of the civilian and legal tradition of Colombia and of its Liberal Party.
sum: Francisco de Paula Santander was a general of Colombian independence and the first great builder of its state. He was vice-president of Gran Colombia and president of New Granada from 1832 to 1837.
